newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish PM healthy at home after minor heart trouble.
newsitem.headline: Finnish PM healthy at home after minor heart trouble.

text.p: Finnish Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen arrived home in Helsinki on Tuesday evening after being treated in a Copenhagen hospital earlier in the day for a heart rhythm problem, a government spokesman said.
"He has arrived in good health," senior government spokesman Asko Mattila, who arrived with the prime minister, said. The prime minister had gone to his official residence in his chauffer-driven car.
An official statement issued in Helsinki earlier on Tuesday afternoon said Lipponen had been released by doctors in the Danish capital after treatment for a heart rhythm disorder.
Lipponen had noticed something was wrong during the night and sought treatment straight away, Mattila, who had been travelling with the prime minister, said.
A former swimmer and waterpolo player, Lipponen, 55, has generally been in good health since becoming prime minister in April 1995.
In June this year, he missed a European Union summit due to a stone in the urinary tract, a painful but not dangerous condition.
Lipponen, a Social Democrat, was in Denmark to attend a meeting of the Nordic Council in Copenhagen when he fell ill on Tuesday.

He was unable to attend the day's meetings with Nordic and Baltic heads of government, and was replaced by Foreign Minister Tarja Halonen, who was at the conference, the Finnish News Agency STT reported.
